choose.codeTitle: A code is the product's passport
choose.codeLead: You don't need to remember codes: choose by the photo and the code is added to your order for you. For builders, here is what every letter and number means — tap a part of the code.

brand.label: F — FLOSSO
brand.text: The first letter F stands for FLOSSO. Every one of our product codes starts with F.

cat.label: KR — product type
cat.text: The next two letters are the product type. KR is a cornice. The other types are listed below.

model.label: 01 — model number
model.text: 01 is model one. Products of the same type differ in pattern and shape by this number: 01, 02, 03…

height.label: 7 — depth
height.text: The first digit after the dash is the depth: it stands 7 cm off the wall.

width.label: 18 — width
width.text: The last two digits are the width: it shows 18 cm wide on the wall.

choose.summary: So FKR01-718 is a FLOSSO cornice, model 1, 7 cm deep, 18 cm wide.
choose.position: A letter in brackets appears only on ornaments: (T) is the top, (P) the bottom. For example, FIK(T)07-818 is a column top.

items.a: The profile is glued to a flat, clean wall with a special facade adhesive and, if needed, fixed with anchors as well. Joints are filled with sealant, then the surface is painted with facade paint. You can fit it yourself or with a contractor — we're happy to advise.

items.q: How long do foam mouldings last?
items.a: With a protective coat and good facade paint, the mouldings withstand rain, sun and frost and keep their shape for many years. Repainting from time to time is recommended.
Yes. Use acrylic or silicone-based facade paints — any colour works. Solvent-based (nitro) paints dissolve foam, so don't use them.
Yes, we deliver orders. Cost and timing depend on the address and volume — call us to confirm. You can also pick up from the workshop yourself: Namozgoh street, Bukhara.
We accept small orders too. We'll tell you by phone from which volume the wholesale price applies.

Cornices, casings, sills, columns and thermal panels are sold per metre; ornaments are sold per piece. Enter the length you need and the calculator shows the sum right away. We confirm the exact price and discounts by phone.

Large windows and tall walls suit a wider profile (15–18 cm); small windows and narrow walls suit a slimmer one (10–12 cm). The easiest start is a ready-made set: its parts are already matched in size.

calc.title: Calculator
calc.lead: Three steps: pick a product, enter the size — the price appears right away. You can send the result with your request.
calc.formula: How it's counted: cornice and sill = window width + 2 × casing width + 10 cm; casing = 2 × window height; casing ornaments are 2 tops and 2 bottoms per window; column = number of columns × height, with 1 top and 1 bottom per column. Metres are rounded up to 10 cm. Each line shows its sum in figures.

FKR.use: Above windows and doors, under the roof and between floors — it finishes the facade at the top.
FKR.tip: A cornice should be wider than the casing: window width + casings on both sides + 5 cm overhang each side.

FNL.use: A frame around windows and doors.
FNL.tip: Small windows suit a 10–12 cm width, large ones 15 cm. Each window needs 2 × its height (both sides).

FPD.use: Under the window — a drip edge and a finish.
FPD.tip: Take the sill the same length as the cornice. A deeper profile projects further from the wall.

FTK.use: The shaft of a column (pilaster) — beside windows, on corners and at entrances.
FTK.tip: Choose the column width (20–40 cm) to suit the facade and take a matching capital and base.

FIK.use: The top (T — capital) and bottom (P — base) of a column.
FIK.tip: The option matches the column width: 20, 30 or 40 cm. Each column needs one top and one bottom.

FIN.use: Ornaments for the top and bottom ends of a window casing.
FIN.tip: The option matches the casing width: 10, 12 or 15 cm. Each casing needs one top and one bottom piece.

FTP.use: A panel for cladding the wall and keeping heat in.
FTP.tip: 30 or 40 cm wide. We'll work out the metres from your wall area — give us a call.
